explain.say: Commas have four main jobs. Look at the first group on the board: lists. I bought rice, beans and eggs. The commas separate the things. Can you list three fruits with commas?

draw.name: x-sort
draw.question: Which job is the comma doing?

explain.say: Now the second group: after an opener. After lunch, we played. The comma comes after the starting bit, so you take a little breath. Try it: Suddenly, the lights went out!

draw.name: x-sort
draw.question: Which job is the comma doing?

explain.say: The third group holds extra information. Ali, my cousin, loves chess. See how the commas wrap the extra bit like a hug? Take it out and the sentence still works: Ali loves chess.

draw.name: x-sort
draw.question: Which job is the comma doing?

explain.say: Last group: talking to someone. Let's eat, Grandma. Yes, Mum. The comma comes before or after the name of the person you speak to. Well done, comma hero! Challenge: add commas to I packed a torch a map and some biscuits.

faq.q: When do I use a comma?
faq.a: Use commas to separate things in a list, after an opening word or phrase, around extra information, and before or after the name of someone you are speaking to.

faq.q: Do I put a comma before and in a list?
faq.a: In British school English you usually don't: rice, beans and eggs. Many American writers do, called the Oxford comma: rice, beans, and eggs. Both are fine if you are consistent.

faq.q: Why does a comma change the meaning?
faq.a: A comma shows where to pause and which words belong together. Let's eat, Grandma talks to Grandma; without the comma, Grandma becomes the food.

faq.q: Can I join two sentences with just a comma?
faq.a: No. That mistake is called a comma splice. Use a full stop, or add a joining word: It was late, so we went home.

faq.q: What does a comma do when I read aloud?
faq.a: It tells you to take a short pause, shorter than a full stop. That helps the listener follow the sentence.
asks: How long is a comma pause?

facts: The Oxford comma, the comma before and in a list, is named after the style of Oxford University Press.
The word comma comes from a Greek word meaning a piece cut off.

quiz.say: Which sentence uses commas correctly in a list?
quiz.show: Which sentence uses commas correctly in a list?

options.show: We saw lions, zebras and giraffes.
options.say: We saw lions, zebras and giraffes.

options.show: We saw, lions zebras and giraffes.
options.say: We saw, lions zebras and giraffes.

options.show: We saw lions zebras, and, giraffes.
options.say: We saw lions zebras, and, giraffes.

quiz.why: Commas separate the items: lions, zebras and giraffes.

wrong.1: The comma should go between the animals, not after saw.
wrong.2: Commas around and break the list in odd places.

quiz.say: Where does the comma go? After school we played football.
quiz.show: Where does the comma go? After school we played football.
quiz.why: Put the comma after the opening phrase, After school.

wrong.0: The opener is After school, so the comma comes after both words.
wrong.2: This splits the subject from its verb.
